message.content: The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has an estimated mass of about 6–7 Jupiter masses (roughly 2 × 10²⁴ kg). Its radius is estimated to be around 1.5–2 times that of Jupiter, making it one of the most massive “planet‑like” objects ever found. However, because it is still forming and may be more accurately described as a protoplanet, its exact classification remains a topic of discussion among astronomers.
